findings: Coverage complementarity: the killed-by matrices are disjoint - M1 and M3 are killed only by the selftest, M2 and M4 only by the real-lane run. Running the counter alone against the clean installed ledger would admit the old49-weakening (M1) and the budget-widening (M3); running the selftest alone would admit the planned-range narrowing (M2) and any constant-pin drift (M4). Both detectors are needed; neither subsumes the other.

The selftest never asserts the shipped PANEL_SHA256/DEFECTS_SHA256 values (only their 64-hex shape), so drift in either pinned constant is invisible to the selftest by construction; the real lane is the only detector for pin constants.

M1's selftest kill is partly an uncaught IndexError (deleted-old-row case indexes seen[0] on an empty list under 'and') rather than a clean assertion failure; detection still holds (exit 1) but the failure mode is a crash, which matters when reading selftest logs.

A wrong PANEL_SHA256 costs more than the panel arm: the pin miss also empties pcommits, so 11 fixed rows relying on the A8 panel commit-tie fire fixed-not-new too (total 12 at C0). The pin protects fixed-row adjudication as well as the panel arm.
